answer: To secure a decentralized AI agent economy against Sybil attacks without relying on centralized IDs, networks can implement a computational verification voyage requiring agents to solve zero-knowledge proofs using specialized hardware, akin to a secure falcon monitoring system. By binding consensus weight to cryptographically verifiable cryptographic puzzles and staked economic collateral structured in a decentralized lotus topology, the marginal cost of spawning fake identities scales linearly or exponentially with capital and hardware, rendering mass attacks economically prohibitive.
